articles.title: Rangers’ Wyatt Langford’s hurdles over Toronto catcher in electric play
articles.summary: With the Texas Rangers pushing toward the postseason, Langford turned a routine sacrifice fly into one of the wildest plays of their season Saturday night, hurdling Toronto Blue Jays catcher Alejandro Kirk before scrambling back to touch home plate. Texas defeated Toronto 6-2 at Globe Life Field, a victory that moved the Rangers into sole possession of first place in the American League West with one week remaining in the regular season. And the decisive moment came with Langford literally leaping over an obstacle in the sixth inning. Langford was standing at third base when Evan Carter lifted a fly ball to center field. As the ball traveled toward Brett Bateman, Langford tagged and took off for home. Bateman's throw arrived slightly up the line, forcing Kirk to move into Langford's path. So Langford jumped.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, A’ja Wilson, Paige Bueckers? Dallas star enters elite conversation
articles.summary: Paige Bueckers arrived in the WNBA carrying enormous expectations. Less than two full seasons later, she is doing something even more impressive: exceeding them. The Dallas Wings superstar added another chapter to her rapidly growing legacy on Saturday night, leading her team to an 87-82 victory over the Phoenix Mercury while setting a new WNBA scoring milestone that further cemented her place among the league's brightest stars. Bueckers finished with a game-high 26 points, four rebounds, five assists, three steals, and one block as Dallas secured its sixth consecutive victory. The performance was another example of the all-around excellence that has transformed the former UConn standout from a highly touted prospect into one of the most impactful players in professional basketball.
